title: networking-streaming-overhead-analysis
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the networking + streaming overhead benchmark results and profiling notes from the Feb 2025 investigation. Focus areas: HTTP/1.1 chunked responses vs HTTP/2 gRPC streaming, chunk size effects, backpressure behavior, and proxy (Envoy) impact. Goal is to decide default transport for our client SDKs and to recommend runtime and proxy tweaks for hosted/Dedicated.
content_2:
Test environment:
- Model: small autoregressive test model (toy-1024) serving continuous token streaming to isolate networking overhead from heavy model compute.
- Inference host: c6g.4xlarge-equivalent (8 vCPU), with 1 GPU mock; kernel patched to mimic our runtime batching.
- Client: 4 client VMs generating steady concurrent streams (N=64 concurrent sessions).
- Network: intra-region (low latency, ~1-3ms RTT), tests additionally run through an Envoy proxy (v1.30) to simulate edge load-balancing.
- TLS: mTLS enabled on proxy tests; direct tests used direct TLS.
- Measurement window: 10 minutes steady-state per config; warmup 2 minutes. Metrics captured: time-to-first-byte (TTFB), token inter-arrival latency, per-stream throughput (tokens/s), CPU and memory on server and proxy, p50/p95/p99 latencies for first-token and whole-stream completion.

Methodology:
- Implemented three transport variants: (A) gRPC streaming (HTTP/2), (B) HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding, (C) HTTP/1.1 streaming via SSE-like framing.
- Controlled chunk sizes: small (256-512 B), medium (1-4 KB), large (16 KB).
- Backpressure scenarios: well-behaved client (read promptly), misbehaving client (delayed reads causing server socket write buffer pressure), and bursty client (rapidly opening new streams).
- Proxy configs: Envoy default (HTTP/2 multiplexing on upstream), Envoy tuned (increased max-concurrent-streams, higher upstream_window_size, reduced flush_interval).
content_3:
Key findings (numbers are averages across multiple runs):
1) gRPC streaming (no proxy)
   - TTFB mean: 32 ms; p95: 110 ms; p99: 220 ms
   - Per-host token throughput (64 concurrent streams): 620 tokens/s
   - CPU overhead: ~12% of CPU cycles attributable to network stack and framing vs baseline idle model-run
   - Observations: Consistent small packet sizes handled efficiently by HTTP/2; low tail latencies.
content_4:
2) HTTP/1.1 chunked (no proxy)
   - TTFB mean: 54 ms; p95: 180 ms; p99: 360 ms
   - Per-host token throughput: 510 tokens/s
   - CPU overhead: ~18% attributable to chunk framing and more frequent syscalls for small chunks
   - Observations: Frequent small writes cause syscall overhead and Nagle interactions (even with TCP_NODELAY set we saw batching at network stack). Coalescing into larger chunks improves throughput but increases per-token latency distribution for early tokens.
content_5:
3) gRPC + Envoy (default config)
   - TTFB mean: 45 ms (+13 ms vs direct); p95: 150 ms (+40 ms)
   - Throughput: 560 tokens/s (-10%)
   - Proxy CPU: Envoy CPU increased notably under small-chunk workloads; observed up to 20% CPU consumption on proxy host for same request load.
   - Observations: Envoy adds serialization and buffering cost; Envoy's flush policy and upstream_window_size materially affect tail latency.

4) HTTP chunked + Envoy
   - TTFB mean: 76 ms (+22 ms vs direct); p95: 240 ms
   - Throughput: 460 tokens/s
   - Observations: Worst combination for tail latency. Envoy's HTTP/1.1 proxying paths add extra copy/assembly steps and backpressure behavior is amplified.
content_6:
Chunk size experiments:
- Small chunks (~256 B): highest CPU and worst p95/p99; ~15-20% lower throughput than medium chunks.
- Medium chunks (1-4 KB): best throughput / reasonable latency tradeoff. p95 improves ~18% vs small chunks.
- Large chunks (16 KB): throughput slightly higher but TTFB for first token increased because we buffer more before flush; not suitable for low-latency streaming features.

Backpressure behavior:
- Well-behaved clients: both transports sustain target; gRPC shows smoother token timing.
- Slow/misaligned clients: with HTTP chunked the server accumulates data in socket buffers and CPU increases due to blocking write attempts and retries; gRPC's flow-control (HTTP/2) provides better backpressure signalling and avoids unbounded buffering on server side.
- Bursty opens: Envoy has limits on concurrent streams; default values caused queueing and increased accept latency. Tuned max-concurrent-streams partially mitigates.
content_7:
Profiling notes:
- System-level flamegraphs show more time in epoll/syscall paths for HTTP/1.1 chunked under small-chunk conditions.
- gRPC traces show more time in HTTP/2 frame assembly but fewer syscalls due to more efficient batching in the kernel.
- Envoy hotspot: buffer allocation and http codec path (vhost/route) and flush/scheduling.
- Recommendation: attach jemalloc profiling and track per-request allocation across path to quantify copy overhead for proxy scenarios.
content_8:
Recommendations:
1) Default transport: gRPC streaming (HTTP/2) for low-latency interactive features. Better tail-latency and backpressure handling.
2) For customers unable to use gRPC (some mobile/web constraints), prefer HTTP/1.1 with medium-sized chunks (1-4 KB) and explicit flush points to balance latency and throughput. Document chunk-size guidance in SDKs.
3) Proxy (Envoy) tuning for hosted/Dedicated:
   - Increase http2 upstream_window_size to reduce early stalls for many small frames.
   - Set higher max-concurrent-streams for fronting proxies handling inference traffic.
   - Adjust flush_interval and write buffer sizing to avoid per-token syscalls.
   - Monitor proxy CPU and configure autoscale thresholds specifically for streaming endpoints.
4) SDK changes:
   - Default to gRPC streaming for official SDKs; fallback to HTTP chunked only when necessary.
   - Implement client-side pacing and recommended read loop behavior to avoid backpressure pathology.
5) Further work:
   - Run tests across WAN (higher RTT/packet loss) to quantify global tail effects.
   - Add dedicated Envoy-specific bench harness that varies concurrency, chunk size, TLS ciphers, and http2 window sizes automatically.
   - Instrument live traffic for first-token TTFB and token inter-arrival histograms to validate in-production behaviour before changing defaults.
content_9:
Action items:
- [ ] PR to SDKs to prefer gRPC by default and add chunk-size config (owner: Priya) -- github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/234
- [ ] Envoy config proposal for hosted fleet (owner: Liam) -- draft in linked_confluence page
- [ ] Add jemalloc + eBPF flamegraph run for Envoy path (owner: Diego)

Appendix: sample bench command lines:
- loadgen (gRPC streaming): ./bench/loadgen --transport grpc --concurrency 64 --chunk-size 1024 --duration 600s --model toy-1024
- loadgen (HTTP chunked): ./bench/loadgen --transport http_chunked --concurrency 64 --chunk-size 1024 --duration 600s

Notes and open questions:
- We used toy-1024 to control compute variance; need to re-run with a medium model (13B) to confirm compute/network ratio effects.
- Need to evaluate mobile/web proxies and browser-based SSE limitations for HTTP chunked path.
- Decide SLA implications before flipping defaults for hosted customers.

If reviewers want the raw CSVs and flamegraphs, they are attached in the JIRA ticket JIRA-RT-4123 (linked above).
